description: Command reference for the network and security platforms most often met in the field. Commands are grouped by task so the same question can be answered on any platform, and the search looks across every vendor at once.

vendors.name: Aruba AOS-CX
vendors.description: Current Aruba switch operating system. Configuration is committed as you type and saved with write memory.

commands.description: Model, serial number, uptime, resource usage.
Status of every port in one table.
Detail and counters for one port.

commands.command:
interface 1/1/24
 no shutdown
 vlan trunk native 999
 vlan trunk allowed 10,20,30
commands.description: Trunk port with an explicit allowed list.

vendors.name: Aruba AOS-S (ProCurve)
vendors.description: Older ProCurve and Aruba 2530 or 2930 line. VLAN membership is expressed from the VLAN, not from the port.

commands.description: Create a VLAN and add access ports as untagged members.
Add a VLAN to a trunk by tagging it on the uplink port.

vendors.name: Cisco IOS and IOS-XE
vendors.description: Catalyst switches and ISR routers. Configuration is applied immediately and lost on reload unless written to startup-config.

commands.description: Model, IOS version, uptime, last reload reason.
Active configuration. Add | section interface to narrow it.
One line per interface: address, status, protocol.
Switch view: port, VLAN, duplex, speed, type.
Counters and errors for one port.
CRC, collisions and drops across all ports in one table.
What is consuming the control plane.
Serial numbers of the chassis and every module.
VLAN database and which ports are in each VLAN.
Learned MAC addresses with port and VLAN.
Locate one device on the switch.
Trunk ports, native VLAN and allowed VLAN list.
Root bridge, port roles and states for one VLAN.
Directly connected Cisco devices with their addresses.
Routing table with the source protocol of each route.
Which route would be used for one destination.
BGP peers, state and prefix counts.
Leases issued when the device is the DHCP server.
Create a VLAN and name it.

commands.command:
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/5
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast
 spanning-tree bpduguard enable
commands.description: Standard access port for an end device.

commands.command:
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30
commands.description: Trunk with an unused native VLAN and an explicit allowed list.

commands.command:
interface Vlan10
 ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
commands.description: Switched virtual interface for inter VLAN routing.
Relay DHCP broadcasts to a server, applied on the client side interface.
Make this switch the root bridge deliberately.
Persist the configuration. write memory does the same.
Test from a specific source interface.
PoE budget and per port consumption.
Cable length and fault distance. Read with show cable-diagnostics tdr.
Live debugging. Always follow with undebug all.

vendors.name: Cisco Meraki
vendors.description: Cloud managed. There is no configuration CLI: the dashboard and its API own the configuration, and the device shell exists only for local diagnosis when a unit will not connect.

commands.description: Local status page, reachable from a client on the device LAN even with no cloud connectivity. Shows uplink state, cloud reachability and firmware.
Factory reset and re-enrolment. The serial stays bound to the organisation.

commands.command: Network wide, Clients, then a client, then Ping and Traceroute
commands.description: Runs the test from the device rather than from your workstation, which is usually the question.

commands.command: Security and SD-WAN, Appliance status, Tools, Packet capture
commands.description: Capture on the appliance, downloadable as pcap.
Association, DHCP and policy events, filterable per client.
Time domain reflectometry per pair, from the dashboard.
List organisations. Everything else needs the organisation identifier from here.
Every device, with serial, model, network and address.
Clients seen in the last day.
Live port status, including PoE draw and errors.

vendors.name: Extreme Networks EXOS
vendors.description: Switches from the Extreme and former Enterasys lines. Configuration applies immediately and is saved explicitly; VLANs are named rather than referred to only by number.

commands.description: System state, uptime, temperature and the configuration in use.
Port state without the auto refreshing display.
VLANs with their tagged and untagged members.
Create a VLAN. The name is how it is referred to afterwards.

commands.command: configure vlan USERS add ports 1-10 untagged
configure vlan USERS add ports 49 tagged
commands.description: Add the VLAN to an uplink.
Routing has to be enabled per VLAN.
Persist. Configuration is live before this but not durable.

vendors.name: Fortinet FortiOS
vendors.description: FortiGate firewalls. The CLI complements the web interface and is where diagnostics actually happen.

commands.description: Packet capture. Verbosity 4 shows interfaces, l prints local time.

commands.command:
diagnose debug flow filter addr 10.0.0.5
diagnose debug flow show function-name enable
diagnose debug flow trace start 20
diagnose debug enable
commands.description: Trace how a packet is processed, including which policy matched and why it was dropped. The single most useful FortiGate command.

commands.command:
diagnose debug disable
diagnose debug reset

config system interface
 edit port1
 set ip 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 set allowaccess ping https ssh
 next
end
commands.description: Address an interface and choose which management protocols it answers.

commands.command:
config router static
 edit 1
 set gateway 192.168.1.254
 set device port1
 next
end

config firewall policy
 edit 0
 set srcintf lan
 set dstintf wan1
 set srcaddr all
 set dstaddr all
 set service HTTPS
 set action accept
 set nat enable
 next
end
commands.description: Policy with source NAT. edit 0 assigns the next free identifier.
Back up the configuration before any change.

vendors.name: HPE Comware
vendors.description: The H3C derived operating system on HPE FlexNetwork and FlexFabric switches. Not to be confused with Aruba AOS-S or AOS-CX, whose syntax is entirely different.

commands.description: Enter configuration mode. The equivalent of configure terminal.

commands.command:
interface GigabitEthernet 1/0/5
 port link-type access
 port access vlan 10
 quit

interface GigabitEthernet 1/0/24
 port link-type trunk
 port trunk permit vlan 10 20 30
 quit
commands.description: Trunk with an explicit allowed list.
Routed VLAN interface. The mask is given as a prefix length.
Counters and errors for one port.
Zero the counters before a test.

vendors.name: Juniper JunOS
vendors.description: Candidate configuration model: changes are staged and only applied on commit, with commit confirmed as a safety net.

commands.description: Enter configuration mode on the candidate configuration.

commands.command: set interfaces ge-0/0/5 unit 0 family ethernet-switching vlan members USERS
commands.description: Access port in a named VLAN.

commands.command: set interfaces irb unit 10 family inet address 10.10.10.1/24

commands.description: Difference between the candidate and the active configuration. Always run before committing.
Apply and roll back automatically in five minutes unless confirmed. Use it on remote devices.
Return to the previous committed configuration.

vendors.name: Linux firewalling and traffic control
vendors.description: nftables and its predecessor iptables, plus the routing and shaping tools. Useful whenever the appliance in front of you turns out to be Linux underneath, which most of them are.

commands.description: The whole rule set, in the syntax that would recreate it.
With handles, which is what you need to delete a specific rule.

commands.command: nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 22 accept
commands.description: Add a rule at the end of a chain.

commands.command: nft delete rule inet filter input handle 12

commands.description: Live rule evaluation, after marking packets with a trace rule.
Filter table with counters and line numbers.
Connection tracking table, the equivalent of a state table.
Every routing table, not just the main one.
Policy routing rules, which decide which table is consulted.
Which route and source address would actually be used.
With statistics, including drops and overlimits.
Socket summary: how many are open, in which states.

vendors.name: Linux networking
vendors.description: Useful when the appliance you are troubleshooting is really a Linux box, which most of them are.

commands.description: Listening sockets with process. Replaces netstat.
Effective DNS configuration per link on systemd hosts.
Targeted capture. -w file.pcap to open it in Wireshark later.
Traceroute and continuous loss measurement in one report.
Follow the resolution from the root down.
Speed, duplex and link detection at the driver level.

vendors.name: MikroTik RouterOS
vendors.description: Menu based CLI where every command is a path. Powerful and inexpensive, with defaults that need review before production.

commands.description: Full configuration as commands, without defaults.
Live per flow bandwidth on an interface.

vendors.name: Palo Alto PAN-OS
vendors.description: Next generation firewalls. Configuration is a candidate that only takes effect on commit, and the CLI has two modes: operational for looking, configure for changing.

commands.description: Model, serial, PAN-OS version, uptime, management address.
Live process and memory view, in top format.
Cluster role and whether the peers agree.
Every interface with its zone, address and state.
Routing table for the default virtual router.
Live sessions from one host. The first thing to look at when traffic is not passing.
Everything about one session: rule matched, application, NAT, decryption.
The security rule base as it is actually being evaluated.

commands.command: test security-policy-match from trust to untrust source 10.0.0.5 destination 8.8.8.8 protocol 6 destination-port 443
commands.description: Asks the firewall which rule a hypothetical packet would match. Answers most policy questions without generating traffic.

commands.command: test nat-policy-match from trust to untrust source 10.0.0.5 destination 8.8.8.8 protocol 6 destination-port 443
show counter global filter severity drop
commands.description: Why packets are being discarded, by reason. The fastest route to a silent drop.

commands.command:
debug dataplane packet-diag set filter match source 10.0.0.5
debug dataplane packet-diag set filter on
debug dataplane packet-diag set capture stage receive file rx.pcap
debug dataplane packet-diag set capture on
commands.description: Packet capture on the dataplane, filtered. Turn it off again with set capture off and clear the filter.
Management plane log, for commit and configuration problems.

commands.command: show log traffic direction equal backward

commands.description: Enter configuration mode on the candidate configuration.

commands.command: set network interface ethernet ethernet1/1 layer3 ip 192.168.1.1/24
set rulebase security rules allow-web from trust to untrust source any destination any application web-browsing service application-default action allow
commands.description: A security rule. application-default is the safer choice over any service.
Apply the candidate. Nothing takes effect before this.
When a partial commit is blocked by an unrelated validation error.

vendors.name: Stormshield SNS
vendors.description: French firewalls, common in public sector and industrial estates. The CLI uses the same object model as the administration suite, and configuration is applied per module rather than through a global commit.

commands.description: Model, firmware, serial, uptime and licence state.
The filter and NAT rules of a policy slot.
Capture, as on any BSD based system.
Follow the filter log live, which shows the rule identifier that matched.
Validate a policy before activating it.
Every system property, useful when comparing two appliances.
Take a configuration backup before any change.
Restore factory settings from the console. Destructive.

vendors.name: Ubiquiti UniFi and EdgeOS
vendors.description: UniFi devices are normally driven by the controller; the CLI is for adoption problems and diagnostics. EdgeOS uses a commit and save model.

commands.description: Model, firmware, adoption status and controller address.
Point a device at a controller. Repeat once the device appears as pending.
Detailed status including uplink and radio state.
Configuration as a flat list of set commands, easy to copy.

commands.command: set interfaces ethernet eth1 vif 10 address 10.10.10.1/24

commands.description: Apply, persist, then leave configuration mode. Commit without save is lost on reboot.

vendors.name: Windows networking
vendors.description: The commands run from the machine in front of you, in their modern PowerShell form with the legacy equivalent where it is still faster.

commands.description: Address, gateway and DNS per interface. Replaces ipconfig /all.

commands.command: Get-NetAdapter | Format-Table Name, Status, LinkSpeed, MacAddress

commands.description: ARP and neighbour cache. Legacy: arp -a.
Listening sockets with owning process. Legacy: netstat -ano.
TCP reachability with route and source information.
Query a specific resolver to separate client cache from server data.
Flush the resolver cache. Legacy: ipconfig /flushdns.
Traceroute with per hop loss statistics.
Generate a full wireless connectivity report.
Built in capture with no software to install. Stop with netsh trace stop.

vendors.name: pfSense and OPNsense
vendors.description: FreeBSD based firewalls. The web interface owns the configuration; the shell is for diagnosis, and the underlying tools are pf and FreeBSD rather than anything vendor specific.

commands.description: The loaded rule set, as pf sees it after the web interface has generated it.
Counters: state table size, searches, matches, and packets dropped.
Capture on an interface. Use pflog0 to see only what the firewall blocked.
Everything pf is dropping, with the rule number that dropped it.
State entries for one host, to see whether a session was ever established.
Follow the filter log on pfSense. OPNsense uses plain text logs under /var/log/filter.
Regenerate and reload every service configuration.
Edit config.xml safely, with a reload on exit. A last resort.
Opens WAN completely, to recover from a rule that locked you out. Undo it immediately after.
Reset the admin password from the console.
Disable the packet filter entirely. Diagnosis only, and never leave it this way.
